Content:
A mixture is any substance made up of two other substances. We usually think of one of the substances as being mixed into the other, like salt in water.

Content:
Two numbers describe a mixture:

Content:
- the total amount of the mixture itself (in liters, grams, pounds, etc.), and
- the percentage of the mixed-in part.

Content:
We can multiply these two numbers to find the total amount of the mixed-in part:

Content:
[MATH: \textrm{part} = \textrm{percentage} \times \textrm{total}]

Content:
For instance, a [MATH: 24]-ounce bottle of apple juice might be [MATH: 25\%] juice (and [MATH: 75\%] water), in which case it contains [MATH: 0.25 \cdot 24 = 6] ounces of juice.

sections.readable_text: What ratio of [MATH: 20\%] gray paint to [MATH: 60\%] gray paint must be mixed to make [MATH: 50\%] gray paint?

sections.normalized_html:
We will use the following formula:

[MATH: \textrm{part} = \textrm{percentage} \times \textrm{total}]

Since the ratio of the two concentrations has to be the same in any amount of the [MATH: 50\%] concentrated mixture, let's assume we wish to make [MATH: 100] gallons of this mixture.

Let [MATH: x] be the number of gallons of the [MATH: 20\%] gray paint used. Since the total mixture must be [MATH: 100] gallons, the rest of the mixture will consist of [MATH: 100-x] gallons of the [MATH: 60\%] gray paint.

We organize this information in a percentage–total–part table:

% Gray

Total (gal)

Part Gray (gal)

[MATH: 20]

[MATH: x]

[MATH: 0.2 \cdot x]

[MATH: 60]

[MATH: 100-x]

[MATH: 0.6 \cdot (100-x)]

[MATH: 50]

[MATH: 100]

[MATH: 0.5 \cdot 100]

The parts gray in each of the [MATH: 20\%] and [MATH: 60\%] paints add up to the part gray in the [MATH: 50\%] paint:

[MATH: 0.2 \cdot x + 0.6 \cdot (100-x) = 0.5 \cdot 100]

Simplifying this equation, we get:

[MATH: 0.2 ⋅ x + 0.6 ⋅ (100 − x)|= 0.5 ⋅ 100; 0.2x + 60 − 0.6x|= 50; − 0.4x|= − 10]

Multiplying both sides of the equation by [MATH: 10] allows us to solve for [MATH: x,] as follows:

[MATH: 10 ⋅ (− 0.4x)|= 10 ⋅ (− 10); − 4x|= − 100; x|= (− 100)/(− 4); x|= 25]

Thus, [MATH: 25] gallons of the [MATH: 20\%] gray paint must be mixed with [MATH: 100-25=75] gallons of the [MATH: 60\%] gray paint.

The required ratio of the [MATH: 20\%] concentration to the [MATH: 60\%] concentration is therefore [MATH: 25:75,] or [MATH: 1:3 .]
